# Concept
Users lose reminders buried in group chat, face conflicting versions, and experience stale cached reads with hidden status on narrow mobile screens. [S2,S3,S5]
A1 (hypothesis): A shared board will reduce reminder loss and version conflicts for tenants. Test: Run an A/B test comparing shared board to chat; track reminder find rate and version mismatch over a 14‑day period.
shared-board (recommended): Shared board centralizes reminders, enables versioned saves, avoids chat noise, respects tenant scope and duplicate reconciliation.
improve-chat: Chat improvements surface buried reminders (S2) but lack version‑controlled saves (S4) that the approved shared board provides.
no-build: Doing nothing leaves burial, conflicts, stale reads unresolved, worsening household coordination and increasing support tickets.
Metric reminder-saved-and-visible: 85% / 14d / 100 samples; confirmed-visible-saves/eligible-save-attempts; baseline unknown; proxy, not observed impact.
Scope: tenant-view,tenant-save,stale-recovery,duplicate-reconciliation; excludes cross-tenant,offline-write,real-notifications,public-release.
Decision: continue; retain-tenant-isolation.
Handoff arjun-cpto (pending, routine-validation): Conduct an Arjun architecture review (v1) of the shared‑board design before any build; proceed only if no conflicts are found.
